_comment: JSCD1108: shared cd-target cases of the two mail gates' script-file check (scripts/hooks/outgoing-copy-gate.py :: script_run_sends, CDGATE1108, the main agent's approval gate; scripts/email-send-gate.mjs :: scriptRunSends, the sub-agent hard gate). Both follow a literal `cd DIR` target by the same rules: cwd always stays a candidate, DIR comes from the cd's own segment, chained cds, `--` and the options, `~`, and a bare `cd` goes to HOME unless the next head cannot be known. They differ on purpose where the target or the script cannot be known: the python twin is fail-closed (a send), the JS twin is the documented accident gate and judges cwd only, as for `python3 $S/x.py` or a missing file (owner decision 2026-10-20, docs/security-hardening.md, 'Reach'). Every case with py != js names its reason. Invariant, checked from both sides: js true -> py true (the JS twin is never the stricter one). `files`: path -> 'send' or 'harmless', relative to cwd, or to HOME with a '~/' prefix; the body follows the extension (.py: smtplib / print, .mjs: nodemailer / console.log). `{CWD}` in a command is the case's cwd. Runners: scripts/__tests__/cd-target-cases.test.py and src/__tests__/cd-target-cases.test.ts.

cases.name: a literal head glued to a substitution
cases.reason: python marks the substitution inside the word and is fail-closed; flattenSubstitutions splits it off, so JS reads `x` as a literal target and adds cwd/x as a candidate (more candidates, never fewer), harmless here

cases.name: cd -, harmless under cwd
cases.reason: the previous directory cannot be known: python is fail-closed, the JS accident gate judges cwd only

cases.reason: the head may cd again (X="cd /y"), so HOME is not known to be where the script runs: python is fail-closed, the JS accident gate does not follow the cd and judges cwd only (the python rule, mirrored)

cases.name: a missing script
cases.reason: python is fail-closed on a script it cannot read; the JS accident gate judges a missing file on its arguments alone
